title: Choose the visual world for zhong.au
question: The roll assigned Dispatch Interval. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Dispatch Interval
options.lineage: Australian wholesale electricity (NEM) price and dispatch charts
options.thesis: Home reads like one day on the energy market: a price trace, a battery schedule, and the engineer who wrote the optimiser that reads them.
options.viewport: A full-bleed 24-hour interval grid is the ground. Name and tagline sit large on its upper left; an illustrative price trace dips below zero at midday with charge, hold and discharge blocks beneath; 'See the work' sits on the grid.
options.risk: It leans on one project, and the trace is illustrative: if the 'not live data' marking is timid, it reads as an invented metric.

raised.raise: Full-bleed field: the interval grid is the ground of the first viewport, edge to edge, never a chart in a box.
Fixed station order: Ongoing, In progress and Shipped hold fixed positions in one state vocabulary everywhere.
Registration: type, project rows and markers all snap to the interval columns; nothing floats off the grid.
Unit discipline: every repeated element (project, tag, skill group) is one numbered unit at one size.
One continuous sheet: no cards anywhere; the grid runs unbroken from hero to contact.
Honest-data encoding: real data draws solid, illustrative data draws dashed and labelled, so the line itself says 'not live'.

options.label: The Datasheet
options.thesis: Jason documented the way he'd want a part documented: features, applications, description and revision history. The primary source, not a summary.
options.viewport: A page-one masthead with name, role and 'Rev. Nov 2026'; Features, Applications and Description in three ruled columns; a functional block diagram of the homelab as Figure 1.
options.risk: Familiar: the technical-document look is where many engineer sites land, and it drifts toward hairline-and-small-label sameness.

options.label: Shader Portal
options.thesis: The name floats as thin type over a living full-screen shader.
options.viewport: A full-screen shader field, 'Jason Zhong' as one oversized word, thin corner links.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a loader and GPU scene contradict 'fast, private, minimal JS' and bury the work. Loses on both axes.
options.risk: Fights the Lighthouse and reduced-motion requirements by nature.

options.label: Darkroom Safelight
options.thesis: Projects develop through fixed stations under amber light.
options.viewport: An amber field banded like a test strip, projects pegged on a drying line.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a photographer's ritual, not an engineer's, and amber grounds fight AA contrast. Loses on both axes.

options.label: Woodblock Registration
options.thesis: The page prints in registered colour blocks over one keyline.
options.viewport: The page's keyline lands first, then indigo and safflower blocks register in.
options.case: Fuses poorly: three pigments break the one-accent brief, and the craft has no tie to the work. Loses on both axes.
options.risk: Reads as costume rather than Jason's work.

options.label: Ornament Plate Book
options.thesis: Projects as numbered units on a plate of repeatable parts.
options.viewport: A numbered plate of units under a constructed display alphabet.
options.case: Fuses poorly: regional ornament says nothing about infrastructure or local-first software. Loses on both axes.
options.risk: Decorative where the brief asks for restraint.

options.label: Orizuru Fold Sequence
options.thesis: One vermilion sheet folds, step by step, into the finished page.
options.viewport: A vermilion sheet, numbered folds in a margin column, the crane diagram centred.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a drenched vermilion ground breaks the restrained brief, and folding has no tie to the projects. Loses on both axes.

options.label: Provenance Ribbon
options.thesis: One continuous ribbon carries a dated history, known and inferred passages typeset apart.
options.viewport: A red ribbon descending through dated folds: UNSW, work, Now.
options.case: Fuses partly: a dated ribbon suits About, but archival buff and ledger serifs read museum, not engineer. Loses on both axes for Home.
options.risk: The cream-and-serif archive look is a known default.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The developer portfolio everyone recognises, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Centred name and tagline with GitHub and email icons, then a 2×2 grid of project cards with tag pills.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the category by design; your refresh brief asks for 'not a template portfolio'.
